breaker.domain: odd prime q with q not dividing 6
breaker.scaled_form: Break(q) iff Q0 union (Q0+delta)=F_q, delta=1/3, Q0={squares including 0}
breaker.cover_condition: Both sets have (q+1)/2 elements, hence cover iff the intersection count is 1.
case_split: q=3 mod 4 -> intersection=(q+1)/4; equality 1 forces q=3, excluded
q=1 mod 4 and delta square -> intersection=(q+3)/4 >1 for q>=5
q=1 mod 4 and delta nonsquare -> intersection=(q-1)/4; equality 1 forces q=5
breaker.q5_check: delta=2 is nonsquare mod 5; I0={0,1,4}, I1={1,2,3}; union=F_5

capacity.meaning: maximum, over mod-5 phases H, of the longest consecutive r-run with Z_H(r) not congruent 0 mod 5
capacity.sharpness: Every phase has at least one zero per period; H=0 and H=2 have exactly one zero, giving a 9-term nonzero run.
capacity.r1_guard: Deleting the finite native prefix r=0,1 does not change eventual 10-periodic zero sets or their sharp max-gap: each residue class recurs infinitely often for r>=2.

transverse_saturation.definition: Sat(q) iff the union of the three root sets modulo q is F_q^* for odd prime q not dividing 6.
transverse_saturation.bound: Three quadratics contribute at most six roots, so q-1<=6 and q<=7.

mixed_parity_boundary.constraint: u,v distinct and same parity; w opposite parity
mixed_parity_boundary.readout: unordered pair {|w-u|,|w-v|} at a maximizer of |w-u||w-v|
mixed_parity_boundary.proof: All admissible distances are odd and <=k-2. If the largest is <=k-4 the product is <=(k-4)^2. If it is k-2, the opposite-parity point is one step from an endpoint and the second distinct same-parity point is at distance at most k-4. The endpoint construction realizes (k-2)(k-4).
mixed_parity_boundary.theorem: max product=(k-2)(k-4), unique maximizing distance multiset={k-4,k-2}
